subject: Issues with processing data from Bruker FlexImaging

messages.author: cd10a01de86eb52f
messages.subject: Issues with processing data from Bruker FlexImaging
parts:
Good Morning,

I have recently been attempting to utilize Cardinal to work up my imaging data but have been running into errors regarding the data such as the following: 

> data1<- normalize(data,method="rms")
> data1a<- process(data1)
Error: BiocParallel errors
  element index: 270, 271, 272, 273, 274, 275, ...
  first error: cannot allocate vector of size 5.8 Mb
In addition: Warning message:
stop worker failed:
  attempt to select less than one element in OneIndex
Err> o i srilie(at, node$con) : error writing to connection
Calls: local ... .send -> <Anonymous> -> sendData.SOCKnode -> serialize
Execution halted

I had originally wondered if it was a problem with my RAM since in previous attemptsit said it couldn't allocate 40 GB but with seeing this as a lower value I'm unsure now. I had pulled the data into an .imzML from FlexImaging as the processed but not normalized data and those files are about 2-10GB in size and had been able to run in Metaspace so I am unsure of where I might be going wrong.

Any help or ideas would be much appreciated!

Best,

Emily

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Issues with processing data from Bruker FlexImaging
parts: It may be a memory issue as normalize() will return a dense vector for each mass spectrum rather than preserving the sparse representation, so the result will be much larger than the original dataset. In such situations, it is intended to chain normalize() directly into a processing step that reduces the dimension, like peakPick().

messages.author: cd10a01de86eb52f
messages.subject: Re: Issues with processing data from Bruker FlexImaging
parts:
I ran a sequence with normalize, smoothSignal, reduceBaseline, and peakPick and originally it was taking hours. I realized that the resolution was detected to 1ppm due to the FT-ICR data and I believe that was part of the issue. I've since set resolution to 100 and ran all of the mentioned steps and it completed no issue.

I think I just will need to play a balancing game of the amount of resolution that my computer can handle working with.

Thank you again for all of your help and quick responses!

~Emily
